page: Amazon Web Services c9g.4xlarge is a compute-optimized server powered by the AWS Graviton processor family. Built on the arm64 architecture, it features 16 dedicated physical cores using the AWS Neoverse-V3 model running at 3.3 GHz. The processor includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. It operates on the Nitro hypervisor and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 8 Gbps. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark data indicates strong performance in specific single-threaded and memory-bound operations. The server achieves top-tier results in single-threaded gzip compression at 36.52 GB/sec and single-threaded bzip3 decompression at 17.33 GB/sec. Passmark memory testing places the system in the top tier with a score of 4296.88, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is rated as strong at 256.09 GB/sec. For database workloads, Passmark database operations score 29409.23, which is categorized as strong. However, stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU performance benchmarks fall within the average tier.

The instance is designed for workloads that benefit from dedicated physical cores and high memory bandwidth, such as static web serving, where it achieves a strong throughput of 54.43 GB/sec. It also supports small-scale machine learning tasks, demonstrating top-tier text generation speeds of 422.27 tokens/sec for a 135M parameter model and strong text generation of 30.52 tokens/sec for a 7B parameter model. The absence of local storage and GPU hardware limits its utility for heavy storage-bound databases or large-scale deep learning training. The arm64 architecture offers a cost-efficient alternative to x86-64 instances for compatible software stacks, delivering high resource density and specialized instruction support like AES cryptography.
